content:
Hello! I'm thinking of contributing to the documentation effort (https://github.com/leanprover-community/iris-lean/issues/84), partly as a way of learning Iris and Lean, partly as a way of trying to pave the way for future users and contributors.

Do we currently build a docs website (using doc-gen4) and deploy it somewhere? I tried https://leanprover-community.github.io/iris-lean_docs/ but there's nothing there.
Hi! Glad to hear you're interested in helping out. How familiar are you with Iris?
Still a newbie at this point, but I'm going to the Iris workshop in Vienna next month, so I'm doing everything I can to ramp up my knowledge in preparation for that
Oh nice! You'll see quite a few iris-lean people there.

You're free to try writing some docs if you want, but I think it might be challenging without experience in Iris. At the moment, I think Rocq is still probably the best way to learn Iris.

If you're looking to get your hands dirtier, one docs task that would be super useful is to help with our rocq_alias annotation effort. We have attributes to tag how the Iris-Lean lemmas relate to Rocq, so learning Iris in Rocq and then trying to annotate what the lemmas are in Lean might be a good learning exercise.
Feel free to do either though! If you write good docstrings I'll be happy to merge them too :)
